facts.evidence: I ran the generator into the scratch folder (scipy/tifffile installed under pylib/): reference.tif 1600x1600 uint16 5,120,256 B (Fiji title strip says '1600x1600 (1600x1600); 16-bit; 4.9MB'), query.tif 520x520 541,056 B (Fiji: '520x520 ... 528K'). ground_truth.json: rotation 12.0 deg, zoom 2.0, pixel sizes 0.65 and 0.325 um/px, offset b_px=(700.06, 606.11) in the 1600x1600 frame, crop centre (800,760). My ground-truth overlay (scratch fixture_out/overlay_gt_800.png) shows the same blob cluster position as Fiji F3. Recorded result in N4/N5/F-log: rotation_deg=12.1721, scale=1.0024, offset_y_px=700.3293, offset_x_px=605.5654, bbox_y0y1x0x1=[637,963,597,923], n_nuclei_reference=429, n_nuclei_query=9, matcher=quad, 'done in 12.0s'.

facts.statement: The fixture 'nuclei' are Gaussian blobs on black (about 450 blobs in the reference, about 9 in the query), not realistic microscopy; the real 2D_QC.jpg is a different dataset.
facts.evidence: make_nucleisky.py: n=450 blobs, radius 5-9 px, gaussian_filter, noise 0.01. Rendered query (scratch fixture_out/query.png) shows 9-10 soft round blobs. 2D_QC.jpg shows real epithelial-like nuclei with background haze; its crop and the Tools fixture have no common data. NucleiSky README/docs give no provenance, licence or credit for the 2D_QC image data (grep acknowledg/credit/courtesy/dataset: no hit).

=== D. LICENCES AND RE-HOSTING ===
- Own content: every repo that owns a screenshot is MIT (c) Cell Migration Lab: LabConstrictor (doc_source branch has no LICENSE file of its own, repo-level MIT on main), LabConstrictor-Tools (docs/img), NucleiSky (2D_QC.jpg). MIT permits re-hosting and modification of the images as repo content, and the site already does so for Welcome_Notebook.png, N2 and F2 via data/hubs.yaml {repo, path}/{doc_source}, re-encoded to 1000 px JPEG (scripts/lcsite/images.py shrink; PNG/JPEG/GIF only, no SVG). Recreating the interfaces in HTML/CSS involves no copied pixels if built from measured tokens.
- labconstrictor-site has no LICENSE or content-licence statement; LabConstrictor-QuPath has no LICENSE (and no images). No org-level policy was found (.github repo shows images/ and profile/ only).
- Third-party UI designs and marks: napari (BSD-3, official dark theme tokens match the screenshot exactly, so a recreation can cite them; napari logo guidelines at napari.org/stable/community/napari_logo_usage.html and github.com/napari/resources were not readable, so logo reuse is unverified), Fiji (GPLv3 over ImageJ2 BSD-2; no logo policy found; the screenshot shows ImageJ title-bar icons and the text '(Fiji Is Just) ImageJ'), JupyterLab (BSD-3, Project Jupyter; the Jupyter orbit logo is in the Welcome screenshot's menu bar), QuPath (GPLv3; no screenshot). Marks that would appear in a faithful recreation: napari name/welcome canvas and activity icon, Fiji/ImageJ name and toolbar icons, Jupyter logo. The site's existing rule is to show host logos only from data/hosts.yaml (downloaded at build time) next to the name, with the footer statement that logos belong to their owners. Embedding any of the screenshots' fonts is a separate point: the Welcome shot looks like Segoe UI (proprietary, unverified), so do not embed it; the site's own Inter and Bricolage fonts are OFL-licensed (docs/assets/fonts/LICENSE-*.txt).
- Provenance gap: 2D_QC.jpg's nuclei data have no stated source or licence; MIT covers the repo asset but not necessarily the underlying images; the fixture (synthetic, generated by MIT code) has no such issue.
- AGENTS.md/DESIGN.md constraints that bear on screenshots: generated image folders are git-ignored (docs/assets/hubs etc.), pictures need alt text, screenshots of the real product need a caption if they teach, host logos only from hosts.yaml, author-controlled exposure (a NucleiSky image appears on the site only if the app's manifest lists it under screenshots; today only banner.jpg is listed), no second manually maintained description."
risks: Fidelity target is a Linux/Xvfb capture of napari 0.9.2 (PyQt5) and Fiji 2.18/Java 21, not what Windows or macOS users see; the 'recognisable to users' goal would be met only for the structure, not the chrome or fonts.

The napari and Fiji views depict a NucleiSky tool declared only on unmerged branches (bridge-test, claude/*); NucleiSky main and its manifest say notebook-only. A demo that looks like a shipped NucleiSky napari/Fiji integration would overstate the product (hubs.yaml already labels it a prototype).

Real napari viewer in the screenshots is a narrow strip and the default post-run view (N4) is a black canvas with 9 dots; a faithful copy looks weak, an improved copy (wide canvas, additive overlay) is no longer 'the real screenshot'.

Several states needed by the spec have no reference picture (napari loaded-not-run, Fiji first chooser dialog, bottom half of the Fiji form, any NucleiSky2DApp notebook view, QuPath at all); those would be invented.

Fixture 'nuclei' are Gaussian blobs, so the demo will not look like real fluorescence microscopy; 2D_QC.jpg looks real but is another dataset, and its SSIM=0.305 headline and unknown data provenance/licence make it risky to present as this demo's result.

Recorded result values (12.1721, 1.0024, 12.0 s, 429/9, matcher quad) are from one Linux test run; reporting 'scale 1.0024' next to a 2x magnification difference confuses viewers unless explained, and 'done in 12.0s' must not be presented as a live duration.

Third-party marks and GPL/BSD UIs: logo terms for napari could not be read, Fiji/ImageJ and Jupyter marks are in the pictures; reproducing icon sets, the Jupyter logo or Segoe UI in the demo needs a conscious decision; the site has no licence statement of its own and QuPath has none.
